name: aromir_v14_evaluate
purpose: Decision 66 in aromir, 18 Nov 2026 (the parent's task): v1.4's errors measured with aromir's own code. make_evaluation_record.py writes the capstone form of the record from the measurement networks' product-error read; holdouts_for_aromir.py writes hold-outs (a8) and (b) in aromir's layout; `aromir evaluate` runs the measurement networks (converted by make_folders.py) on them; the record aromir ships is written only if every cell agrees with the capstone form to 0.01 cm-1. No quantum chemistry: stored analytic Hessians and three networks. In WSL from ~/aromir_dev (aromir branch release-networks), capped by probes/wsl_capped.sh beside the live search.
command: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -e bash -c "export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 PYTHONUTF8=1; cd /mnt/c/Users/thebr/Documents/CapstonePlan/plans/05_delta-probed-ir-pipeline/probes/results_m1/aromir_v14_release_2026-11-18 && echo '=== (EVAL14) start' && bash ../../wsl_capped.sh 1536 -- /usr/bin/time -f '(EVAL14) max RSS %M kB, wall %e s' bash evaluate.sh /mnt/c/Users/thebr/Documents/CapstonePlan/plans/05_delta-probed-ir-pipeline /home/thebreadishard/aromir-src/src/aromir/releases/v1.3/evaluation.json; echo '=== (EVAL14) done'"

estimate.basis: product_error.py reads each molecule twice (two atom orders); the capstone's read of the same 48 molecules with the same three networks took 102 s on 2 threads (product_error.json run.seconds); aromir's evaluate does the same work plus the hold-outs' writing

memory.basis: a bound: probes/wsl_capped.sh stops the run at 1536 MB; its first launch (18 Nov 08:23) peaked at 0.46 GB (max RSS), the capstone read at 0.37 GB
